answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit in a grove of verified peers before it can trade, like a lotus that only blooms after its roots are checked. A prism of independent attestors scores each agent's past work, and identities with no history earn no trust. Creating a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand deposits plus a thousand track records, so an attacker pays real money for every fake while honest agents reuse one cheap, proven identity.
